headline: Brief Reports Water Levels Rise in Six Dams; Angat at 181.57 Meters
seoTitle: Brief: Six Dams Rise; Angat Reported at 181.57m
seoDescription: An FMB News midday brief reports water levels rising in six major dams, with Angat at 181.57 meters and La Mesa beginning a gradual decline.
deck: The newsroom brief cites a Saturday dam-status update showing gains in six reservoirs, while FMB News keeps the exact August 15 elevations source-attributed pending a directly retrievable PAGASA table.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The FMB News August 15 midday brief reports that water levels rose in six of nine monitored major dams, identifying Angat, Ipo, Ambuklao, San Roque, Pantabangan and Magat among the reservoirs with gains.

The brief places Angat Dam at 181.57 meters above sea level, up 1.47 meters in 24 hours, and says the reservoir had recovered more than 30 meters from a late-July low. It also reports San Roque at 267.40 meters and says La Mesa Dam had begun to decrease gradually.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The email cites two August 15 Inquirer reports based on PAGASA dam monitoring. FMB News could not independently retrieve the corresponding August 15 PAGASA dam-status table during the final publication pass, so the precise elevations and day-on-day changes remain source-attributed rather than independently reproduced.
Dam levels matter both for water supply and for flood-management decisions. A rising reservoir can improve stored-water availability while also requiring close monitoring during sustained rainfall.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Angat is a critical source of water for Metro Manila and irrigation in Central Luzon. Clear, date-specific reservoir data helps households, farmers, water managers and local governments distinguish water-supply recovery from flood-control risk.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for the next PAGASA dam-status bulletin, spillway or gate-operation advisories, rainfall warnings over dam watersheds and any updated La Mesa or Tullahan River flood guidance.
